title: 230. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Constructing Equations from Word Problems
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Translating a verbal statement into a linear equation
questions.learningObjective: Construct a linear equation from a statement about an unknown number.
questions.question: A number increased by \(7\) is \(15\). Which equation represents this statement if the number is \(x\)?
questions.explanation: The phrase "increased by \(7\)" means that \(7\) is added to the unknown number \(x\). Therefore the statement translates to \(x+7=15\). The expression \(x-7=15\) would mean "a number decreased by \(7\) is \(15\)," which is not the given statement.
questions.hint: Identify the operation suggested by "increased by," then write the equation using the unknown \(x\).

questions.concept: Constructing a linear equation from a sum statement
questions.learningObjective: Translate a verbal description involving twice a number into an equation.
questions.question: The sum of twice a number and \(5\) is \(17\). Which equation represents this statement if the number is \(x\)?
questions.explanation: "Twice a number" is \(2x\). The sum of this quantity and \(5\) is \(2x+5\), and this sum equals \(17\). Therefore the equation is \(2x+5=17\). The expression \(2(x+5)\) would mean twice the sum of the number and \(5\), which is not the given statement.
questions.hint: Translate "twice a number" first, then add \(5\) to that expression.

questions.concept: Constructing a perimeter equation from a rectangle problem
questions.learningObjective: Form an equation for the perimeter of a rectangle when one side is expressed in terms of the other.
questions.question: The length of a rectangle is \(3\text{ cm}\) more than its width. The perimeter is \(26\text{ cm}\). Which equation represents this situation if the width is \(w\text{ cm}\)?
questions.explanation: The width is \(w\), and the length is \(w+3\). The perimeter of a rectangle is \(2(\text{width})+2(\text{length})\), so it is \(2w+2(w+3)\). Since the perimeter is \(26\text{ cm}\), the equation is \(2w+2(w+3)=26\). The expression \(w+(w+3)=26\) represents only half the perimeter.
questions.hint: Write the length in terms of the width, then use the perimeter formula for a rectangle.

questions.learningObjective: Form an equation from a constant-speed travel situation.
questions.question: A car travels \(240\text{ km}\) at a constant speed of \(60\text{ km/h}\). Which equation represents the time \(x\) in hours?
questions.explanation: Using \(\text{distance}=\text{speed}\times\text{time}\), the distance traveled is \(60x\). Since the car travels \(240\text{ km}\), the equation is \(60x=240\). The expression \(\frac{x}{60}=240\) divides the time by the speed instead of multiplying, so it does not represent \(\text{distance}=\text{speed}\times\text{time}\).
questions.hint: Recall the relationship \(\text{distance}=\text{speed}\times\text{time}\), and substitute the given values.

questions.concept: Constructing an equation for consecutive integers
questions.learningObjective: Form an equation for the sum of three consecutive integers.
questions.question: The sum of three consecutive integers is \(72\). Which equation represents this statement if the smallest integer is \(n\)?
questions.explanation: If the smallest of three consecutive integers is \(n\), then the next two integers are \(n+1\) and \(n+2\). Their sum is \(n+(n+1)+(n+2)\), and this sum equals \(72\). Therefore the equation is \(n+(n+1)+(n+2)=72\). The expression \(n+(n+2)+(n+4)\) represents three consecutive even or odd integers, not three consecutive integers.
questions.hint: Decide how far apart consecutive integers are, express all three in terms of \(n\), then use the given sum.

questions.learningObjective: Translate an age relationship into an equation involving current and future ages.
questions.question: A father is \(4\) times as old as his son. In \(5\) years, the father will be \(3\) times as old as his son. Which equation represents this situation if the son's current age is \(s\)?
questions.explanation: The father's current age is \(4s\). In \(5\) years, the father's age will be \(4s+5\), and the son's age will be \(s+5\). The statement says the father will then be \(3\) times as old as the son, so \(4s+5=3(s+5)\). The equation \(4(s+5)=3s+5\) mixes up the two relationships: it applies the factor \(4\) to the son's future age and the factor \(3\) to the son's current age.
questions.hint: Write both current ages, then add \(5\) to each age to represent the situation in \(5\) years.

questions.learningObjective: Form an equation for adding pure acid to a solution to reach a target concentration.
questions.question: A \(10\)-liter solution is \(20\%\) acid. If \(x\) liters of pure acid are added, the resulting solution is \(50\%\) acid. Which equation represents this situation?
questions.explanation:
The original solution contains \(0.20(10)=2\) liters of acid. After adding \(x\) liters of pure acid, the total acid is \(2+x\), and the total volume is \(10+x\). The new concentration is \(50\%\), so
\[
\frac{2+x}{10+x}=0.5
\]
which is equivalent to \(2+x=0.5(10+x)\). The expression \(2+x=0.5(10)\) ignores the added volume \(x\).
questions.hint: Find the acid content before and after adding \(x\) liters, then use \(\text{concentration}=\text{acid volume}\div\text{total volume}\).

questions.learningObjective: Form an equation for two pipes filling a tank together.
questions.question: Pipe A fills a tank in \(6\) hours, and pipe B fills the same tank in \(4\) hours. If both pipes are opened together, the tank is filled in \(t\) hours. Which equation represents this situation?
questions.explanation: Pipe A fills \(\frac{1}{6}\) of the tank per hour, and pipe B fills \(\frac{1}{4}\) of the tank per hour. Together they fill \(\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{4}\) of the tank per hour. Since the whole tank is filled in \(t\) hours, their combined rate is also \(\frac{1}{t}\). Therefore the equation is \(\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{t}\). The equation \(6+4=t\) incorrectly adds the times instead of the rates.
questions.hint: Use the work-rate principle: \(\text{combined rate}=\text{sum of individual rates}\), and \(\text{rate}=\text{work done}\div\text{time}\).

questions.concept: Constructing a product equation for consecutive even integers
questions.learningObjective: Form an equation for the product of two consecutive positive even integers.
questions.question: The product of two consecutive positive even integers is \(48\). Which equation represents this statement if the smaller integer is \(x\)?
questions.explanation: If the smaller positive even integer is \(x\), the next consecutive even integer is \(x+2\). Their product is \(x(x+2)\), and this product equals \(48\). Therefore the equation is \(x(x+2)=48\). The expression \(x(x+1)\) would represent the product of two consecutive integers, not two consecutive even integers.
questions.hint: Think about how far apart two consecutive even integers are on the number line.

questions.learningObjective: Form an equation for a faster train overtaking a slower train that started earlier.
questions.question: A train leaves a station traveling at \(80\text{ km/h}\). Two hours later, a second train leaves the same station traveling at \(100\text{ km/h}\) in the same direction. If \(t\) is the time in hours after the second train leaves, which equation represents the moment when the second train catches the first?
questions.explanation: The first train has a \(2\)-hour head start. When the second train has traveled for \(t\) hours, the first train has traveled for \(t+2\) hours. The distance traveled by the first train is \(80(t+2)\), and the distance traveled by the second train is \(100t\). At the catch-up moment, these distances are equal, so \(100t=80(t+2)\). The expression \(80(t-2)\) would incorrectly subtract the head-start time.
questions.hint: Account for the first train's extra \(2\) hours of travel time when writing its distance.
